We dream big but keep things simple to act fast.​If you want to grow with us, make an impact, and shape the future of Ice Cream, this is the place for you!
Main Job Purpose:
The range of Machine Operator roles varies between categories and technologies, but generally sits within the Filling, Forklift and Material & Waste Transfer, Mixer, Packing & Reporting Job Families.
The Machine Operator is responsible for the safe operation of production equipment to deliver customer requirements through completion of the production plan, adhering to quality standards and maximising cost effectiveness, optimal running and equipment efficiency.  She/he is expected to carry out Autonomous Maintenance such as Cleaning Lubrication and inspection activities and record any issues/problems with the equipment which cannot be resolved by themselves to pass to the Technical Operator to resolve.  The Machine Operator should master the operation of a series of production machines within a complete production unit in order to provide factory resilience – this includes set-up, start-up, running, basic issue resolution, changeovers, cleaning (including allergens), inspection, shutdown & general safe working.
Key Skills and Responsibilities:
Technical - Knowledge and application of technical skills to operate machinery safely and effectively in order to meet the production plan.  Conduct inspections, cleaning and lubrication as required.
o    Possesses a basic knowledge of the principals of mechanism, motion and pneumatics.
o    Work to and maintain cleaning and checking standards of machinery responsible for.
o    Understands properties of materials being handled; performs correct adjustment and setting.
o    Proactively works with Professional Maintenance and Quality Control staff to reduce breakdowns and defects.
o    Carry out product and process changeovers/washouts to maintain quality standards whilst minimising the impact to the production plan.
Operational Activities:
o   Start-Up/Shutdown procedures - Carries out pre-start-up checks to ensure that the area and equipment is clean and is in a safe condition. Shuts down machines & equipment and the area.
o   Changeovers – carries out changeovers between products in line with defined standards.
o   Inspection & Issue Resolution – inspecting machines in operation and solving issues that arise to keep the machine running optimally.
o   Cleaning – Keep area & machines clean and tidy in line with defined standards.
o   Material Availability - Provides a continuous supply of appropriate packaging & raw material from local storage areas to the machine.
o   Administration – Conducts effective hand-over activities and records accurately events that have occurred during shift (cases packed/rejects etc).
Safety – Working knowledge of the workplace and the hazards within it. Utilise appropriate safety and environmental procedures relating to the Sourcing Unit and allocated equipment to ensure a safe working environment for the whole team. Machine operators are expected to raise SHE occurrences encountered on shift via safety tags, near miss forms, accident reports and other mechanisms where appropriate.
Workplace Hazards - Full knowledge of workplace and hazards within it.  Utilise appropriate safety and environmental procedures for people, processes, materials, products and equipment relevant to the tasks in your area.
Environment / Waste - Reduce costs due to waste and minimise impact to health, safety and the environment through working to eliminate waste and through the correct management of waste and hazardous materials. Non-conformances to waste standards must be escalated via appropriate supervisory channel.
Quality - Monitors quality against set standards and reports any product, hygiene and packaging faults.  Detects process abnormalities quickly and takes emergency action to prevent them. Machine operators are expected to raise quality non-conformances / risks encountered on shift via appropriate mechanisms.
§  Continuous Improvement – Knowledge and understanding of the key principles of continuous improvement and an awareness of the tools used to identify and prioritise time, cost and waste losses in the production area and eliminate them; role requires data collection.  Monitor measures and performance after initial improvements and take further action as required.
Problem Solving – A Working Knowledge of how to identify, prioritise and address problems using appropriate tools and techniques that eliminate recurrence.  Must demonstrate initiative. Machine operators are expected to resolve issues in their area that are within their skillset.

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We are seeking an Associate Director to join our Global Patient Safety Standards & Training team.
Reporting to the Head of Global Patient Safety (GPS) Standards & Training, this position is responsible for establishing and maintaining procedures and policies consistent with Pharmacovigilance regulatory requirements and industry standards. A key part of the role is close collaboration with the Process and Procedures (P&P) team and support of the Process Owner Network (PONs). The responsibilities of this job are foundational in the creation and maintenance of the Pharmacovigilance (PV) System that is essential in enabling the department, and therefore the company, to comply with regulatory PV requirements in all relevant territories worldwide, and to operate efficiently and effectively in alignment with established industry practices. The role supports GPS activities and ensures procedures remain compliant with applicable global regulations as they evolve.
This position offers the opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, science-driven organization making a meaningful difference to patients worldwide.
When & where:
• Work Location: Uxbridge, UK
• 3 days per week on site
• 25% Travel may be required
Discover your role:
• Ensure that PV Intelligence updates are systematically assessed and reflected in GPS procedures, so that documented processes remain aligned with current regulatory expectations and the procedural framework is maintained in a state of audit and inspection readiness at all times.
• Act as a key liaison to Process & Procedures (P&P) and the Learning Centre of Excellence (LCoE) for procedural updates, so that procedural changes are accurately captured, appropriately sequenced, and correctly reflected in the associated training curriculum.
• As an SME, partner with the Head of GPS Safety Operations to validate that procedures are fit for purpose against safety practices, closing gaps between documented process and operational execution, including the mapping of procedural documents to regulations and to the training curriculum.
• Apply deep PV process design expertise to develop, implement, and maintain GPS procedures in alignment with regulations, Regeneron Standards, and industry best practices — in partnership with Process & Procedures (P&P), Process Owners, and SMEs — and lead the assessment of evolving global PV regulations.
• As a primary liaison to P&P, partner to set risk-based prioritization and sequencing in managing procedural updates across the GPS framework, in partnership with PONs and GPS Functional Leads.
• Assist in ensuring the correct procedural documents are assigned to the relevant training curriculum.
• Maintain oversight of and support for GPS Planned Process Deviations (PPDs), including guiding SMEs on meeting Global Development Quality (GDQ) approval criteria.
• Coordinate with P&P to align PPD expiration dates with queued procedure projects, adjusting prioritization as needed.
• Serve as GPS's escalation point for internal process and quality-event alignment challenges related to procedural updates, working in alignment with senior management and key stakeholders to investigate and resolve non-compliance.
• Manage, alongside the Process Owners, the content of procedures for GPS, escalating material gaps to senior management, including the maintenance and accuracy of PSMF Annex E in relation to GPS procedures.
• Maintain an overview of CAPAs associated with procedures, including those arising from both audits and inspections, and work closely with SMEs, PONs and the P&P team to ensure timely CAPA closure, including allowing appropriate time for associated training.
• Provide regular metrics on CAPAs, process deviations, and training compliance to GPS department leadership.
• Lead initiatives to enhance GPS process effectiveness and efficiency, including the analytical framework for performance metrics, and present findings and recommendations to leadership.
• Liaise regularly with other functional teams e.g. Corporate and Clinical QA on potential impacts to GPS Processes or GXP-related activities.
• Represent Standards & Training in audits and inspections.
• Serve as the back-up GPS Standards & Training liaison to LCoE.

• Minimum Bachelor's degree is required. Education in the life sciences is a strong plus.
• 7+ years' experience of Pharmacovigilance/Drug Safety, Regulatory Affairs or Quality Assurance in the pharmaceutical/biotech industry.
• Thorough understanding of Pharmacovigilance/Drug Safety regulations and PV Quality Management Systems.
• Extensive experience managing procedural updates.
• Experience in PV process design and optimization.
• Track record of successful project management relevant to document management.
• Strong organizational skills.
• Ability to write procedural documents to accepted standards of quality.
• Experience presenting in audits and inspections.
• Ability to work collaboratively across functions with SMEs, process owners and cross-functional partners.

ig.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/ext_ig/job/ci.description_excerpt:
Job Title
Senior Journey Transformation Analyst
Job Description
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
Your Team
• Journey Transformation owns the end-to-end journeys that clients and colleagues move through: onboarding, funding, trading, servicing, disputes and account closure on the client side, and the operational workflows that sit behind all of them.
Your role in the Team’s Success
• Our job is to find where those journeys break, prove what the breakage costs, and drive the fix through to a measured result.
• Digital servicing and conversational AI are one lever we pull. Process redesign, channel change, automation, system configuration, policy change and eliminating steps at source are others. The lever follows the diagnosis, never the reverse.
• You are the engine of that mission. You work out where friction and servicing demand are really coming from, build the evidence for what will remove them, and drive those changes through to delivery and proven results. Working directly alongside the Head of Journey Transformation in a small core team, you will help establish our journey intelligence capability from the ground up: the mapping standards, the diagnostic methods and the evidence bar the team is held to.
• Change runs down two routes. Some is delivered directly within Operations, through our servicing and contact centre technology estate - and you will own that end to end. Some belongs on the roadmaps of other teams, such as app and web product, platform APIs, marketing or compliance, and has to earn its place there on the strength of the evidence behind it - so you will build cases strong enough to do that, then carry them through the governance that prioritises them.
This is not a documentation role. The mandate is change shipped and results proven.
What success looks like
By the end of year one:
• A credible current-state picture exists across our priority journeys, client and operational, to a standard the business trusts and returns to.
• Journey improvement runs as an ongoing cycle rather than a series of projects: a pipeline that always holds the next evidenced opportunity and shipped changes that continue to be optimised against live performance.
• The first changes have delivered proven, sustained improvement against their baselines, with guardrails intact, so friction is genuinely removed rather than moved.
• Success is measured in client and business outcomes, not technology milestones, to an evidence standard Finance signs off without argument.
• Other teams bring their journey problems to us, because the cases we put on their roadmaps delivered for their objectives as well as ours.
What you’ll do:
Diagnose
• Map and analyse end-to-end journeys across both client experiences and internal operational workflows, producing current-state assessments in BPMN or equivalent notation, and quantifying friction through cost, manual effort, error and rework rates, compliance exposure and scalability constraints.
• Lead journey discovery: run deep-dive sessions with operational teams, advisors, team leaders and system owners, capturing qualitative pain points alongside quantitative impact.
• Drive contact and failure demand to root cause, using contact reason data, conversation analytics, operational MI, advisor insight and journey analysis - going beyond what clients ask about to why the journey made them ask.
Build the case
• Own the pipeline of journey improvement and cost-to-serve opportunities: identify, size, prioritise and sequence them into a delivery roadmap and a maintained backlog.
• Build the case for each change: baseline established before any forecast, benefits sized conservatively at marginal cost, delivery route identified, guardrails defined.
• Produce evidence-based business cases with clear ROI, risk assessment and competitive benchmarking, pitched in terms the receiving audience acts on, whether that is Operations, Finance, Product or Compliance.
Deliver
• Translate journey improvements into clear business requirements, functional specifications and user stories, with Jira tickets and traceability maintained from journey finding through to system change.
• Own delivery of in-remit changes end to end, from definition through build to live.
• Broker changes owned by other teams onto their roadmaps through agreed governance, with evidence and a clear articulation of the benefit to their objectives as well as ours.
Prove
• Own performance in life: track every shipped change against its baseline, confirm the improvement is real and sustained before any benefit is claimed, and feed live performance into the next iteration.
• Hold the quality bar. On client journeys, deflection counts only as resolution: repeat contact rates and journey CSAT operate as guardrails on every case. On operational journeys, the equivalent test is that work removed is work eliminated, not work displaced to another team.
• Work closely with the data team on measurement design, with finance partners on benefits realisation, and with frontline advisors and team leaders whose insight is a primary source.
• Operate with awareness of IG's regulatory context, including Consumer Duty outcomes, the needs of vulnerable clients and the demands of a multi-jurisdictional operating model.
What You'll Need:
You can take a messy, real-world journey - client-facing or back-office - and turn it into a clear logical map with a defensible number attached to the friction, then carry the fix through delivery and stand behind the result afterwards.
Diagnostic craft
• Strong experience mapping end-to-end journeys across both customer-facing and operational processes, using BPMN or equivalent notation and tools such as Visio, Lucidchart or Miro.
• Proven ability to run stakeholder interviews and discovery sessions, asking detailed questions about how work actually happens and getting to the answer underneath the first one.
• A data-led approach to root cause: comfortable in contact and operational analytics, and in designing the measurement that will later prove the change worked.
Evidence and outcome ownership
• You establish a baseline before you forecast, size benefits conservatively, and have had your numbers challenged by finance or governance partners and defended them.
• You have owned an improvement outcome through to a measured result, and can speak precisely to the baseline, what landed and how it was…

We’re looking for a Tax Manager to join our Group Tax Reporting team. Reporting to the Director of Group Tax Reporting, you’ll take ownership of hands-on tax provisioning, reporting and compliance activities across multiple jurisdictions.

Although the position carries a manager title, you’ll be directly involved in preparing and reconciling tax provisions, supporting the consolidation process and responding to audit requirements. You won’t simply coordinate work or oversee its completion. You’ll personally deliver key elements of the tax reporting cycle.

What You’ll Do
• Prepare group and statutory tax provisions for financial statement reporting and audits.
• Perform the underlying calculations and reconciliations required to support accurate tax provisions.
• Support the consolidation of tax information from multiple jurisdictions into the group reporting process.
• Prepare supporting schedules, analysis and documentation for internal and external audit requirements.
• Investigate and resolve differences identified through tax provision reconciliations.
• Act as a key contact for direct tax matters across assigned jurisdictions.
• Coordinate with local finance teams and outsourced service providers to support tax compliance obligations.
• Work with external advisers and tax authorities to support tax audits and manage tax risks.
• Assess the accounting impact of relevant tax and regulatory changes.
• Maintain and improve tax reporting processes, controls and supporting documentation.
• Identify opportunities to simplify, standardise or automate tax processes.
• Collaborate with colleagues across Tax, Finance, Legal, Operations and IT.
• Manage competing deliverables across jurisdictions while maintaining clear communication around progress, risks and deadlines.
What We’re Looking For
• A professional qualification such as ACA, ACCA, CTA, CPA or an equivalent accounting or tax qualification.
• Practical experience preparing tax provisions rather than only reviewing or overseeing work completed by others.
• Experience working with tax reconciliations and supporting tax reporting cycles.
• Knowledge of IAS 12 and/or ASC 740 tax accounting principles.
• Experience supporting financial statement audits and responding to audit queries.
• Understanding of direct tax compliance and its interaction with tax accounting and financial reporting.
• Experience working within a multinational organisation, professional services firm or similarly complex international environment.
• Strong analytical skills and confidence working with detailed financial and tax data.
• Experience using Excel and familiarity with ERP platforms such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite or comparable systems.
• Clear communication skills and the ability to work effectively with stakeholders across functions and jurisdictions.
• A proactive approach to managing priorities, resolving issues and meeting reporting deadlines.
What Will Help You Succeed
You’ll enjoy working with the detail and taking personal ownership of technical deliverables. You’ll be comfortable preparing calculations, completing reconciliations, investigating differences and ensuring that your work is accurate and appropriately supported.
You’ll also know when to ask questions, obtain information from others and communicate early when a deadline, dependency or risk requires attention. This role will suit someone who wants to remain close to the technical work while continuing to develop their experience within a global tax environment.
Why Join Us?
You’ll gain broad exposure to group tax reporting across multiple jurisdictions and work closely with colleagues throughout a global organisation. The role offers the opportunity to deepen your expertise in tax provisioning, reporting, compliance, controls and process improvement while making a visible contribution to the Group Tax function.
We welcome applications from candidates with relevant transferable experience. If you meet most, but not every, requirement, we encourage you to apply.

velux.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/velux_reside.description_excerpt:
Great customer journeys start with a great first conversation.
When homeowners begin thinking about improving their home, they often have questions before they know exactly what they need.
This role is about helping them find the right answers.
As an Inbound Consumer Advisor within our Design & Inbound Services team, you'll be one of the first people customers speak to when they contact VELUX. You'll support homeowners and blinds retailers across phone, email, chat and digital channels, helping them understand their options and feel confident about the next step in their project.
That means listening carefully, asking the right questions and providing clear, practical guidance. Sometimes you'll help a customer find the right solution there and then. Other times you'll identify opportunities that are best progressed through our specialist Design Services or Replacement Services teams.
Based in our Glenrothes office, no two conversations are quite the same, but every interaction plays an important role in shaping the customer experience.
What the role involves:
• Being a first point of contact for homeowners and blinds retailers
• Providing clear, simple and accurate advice across phone, email, chat and digital channels
• Understanding customer requirements, project goals and intended outcomes through effective questioning
• Helping homeowners explore products, services and solutions that best suit their needs
• Supporting blinds retailers with telephone orders and ensuring key details are accurately captured
• Translating technical or complex information into easy-to-understand guidance
• Taking ownership of customer enquiries through to resolution or appropriate handover
• Identifying opportunities to recommend products or services that add value to the customer
• Qualifying and transferring appropriate opportunities to Design Services or Replacement Services
• Working closely with colleagues across VELUX to ensure a seamless customer journey
• Keeping customer records and interactions accurate and up to date
• Looking for opportunities to improve the customer experience and ways of working
It's busy, but that's part of what makes it rewarding
Consumer Services is a fast-paced environment where every customer is at a different stage of their journey. Some customers will simply need reassurance they're making the right decision. Others may need guidance through more complex questions around products, installation or project planning.
The role involves balancing quality conversations with service expectations, including customer satisfaction, first contact resolution and responsiveness.
There will be plenty of opportunities to build product knowledge, strengthen commercial awareness and develop confidence in supporting customers through important home improvement decisions.
There is also a real opportunity to influence how we work. If something could be made simpler, clearer or more effective for customers, we want people who are willing to contribute ideas and help drive improvements.
What makes someone successful in this role?
Experience in customer service is important, but attitude and approach matter just as much.
The right person is likely to:
• Enjoy helping people and building customer confidence
• Listen carefully and ask thoughtful questions
• Communicate clearly and avoid unnecessary jargon
• Stay calm and organised in a busy environment
• Take ownership of customer outcomes
• Balance customer needs with commercial opportunities
• Pay attention to detail and maintain high levels of accuracy
• Feel comfortable learning new products, systems and processes
• Work well with colleagues across different teams
• Be open to feedback and committed to continuous improvement
Technical knowledge of VELUX products isn't expected from day one. Training and support will be provided.
What matters most is a genuine desire to help customers, a willingness to learn and the confidence to guide customers towards the right solution.
Why this role matters
Consumer Services is often the front door to VELUX for homeowners and blinds retailers. The quality of these early interactions can shape the customer's perception of our business and influence the success of their project.
By providing clear advice, reducing customer effort and creating confidence from the outset, this role helps deliver an effortless customer experience while supporting future growth through high-quality customer conversations.
Interested?
If you enjoy helping people, solving problems and guiding customers towards the right solution, this role offers the opportunity to make a real difference to both the customer experience and the success of the business.

Engineering leadership
• Lead the modernization engineering team that rebuilds critical middle office applications as cloud-native services on AWS.

AI-augmented delivery
• Design and run the programme's agentic SDLC: AI-assisted reverse engineering of legacy code, spec generation, code conversion, test generation and documentation.
• Choose, combine and orchestrate AI tools (for example GitHub Copilot, Devin, Blitzy and agent frameworks) based on evidence of what works, not tool preference.
• Build reusable agent workflows, prompt libraries and knowledge context (codebase knowledge graphs, vector databases, MCP integrations).
• Track AI productivity and quality (throughput, defect rates, rework, cost per migrated application) and report outcomes to leadership.
Risk, controls and governance
• Put human review checkpoints, audit trails and secure-coding gates on all AI-generated code, in line with State Street technology risk, information security and model governance policies.

• Handle data classification and approved-tool usage for client and confidential data.
People and capability

Required experience and skills
• 12+ years in software engineering, with 5+ years leading large engineering teams on complex modernization or cloud migration programmes.
• Strong hands-on background in Java/Spring Boot, microservices, REST and messaging (Kafka/IBM MQ) and AWS (ECS/EKS, IAM, networking).
• Proven, practical experience using AI coding assistants and agents in delivery, with measurable results.
• Experience migrating legacy stacks (e.g. COBOL, C/C++, PowerBuilder, Sybase) to modern platforms, including database migration to Oracle.
• Working knowledge of CI/CD and DevSecOps (Harness or similar), secrets management (Vault/CyberArk) and observability.
• Experience delivering in a regulated financial services environment with strong change and control requirements.
Preferred
• Knowledge of investment servicing or middle-office areas: trade capture, confirmation, settlement, collateral, reconciliation, investment accounting.
• Experience building MCP servers, knowledge graphs or retrieval-augmented context for engineering agents.
• AWS Professional-level or equivalent certification.
Success measures (first 12–18 months)
• An AI-augmented delivery model running across the programme, with productivity gains measured against a baseline.
• Modernization releases delivered to plan, with no material production incidents at cutover.
• A permanent engineering team in place, able to run and evolve the new cloud-native platform.
• No audit or control findings related to how AI is used in delivery.
Leadership attributes
You make decisions and are comfortable with ambiguity. You're credible both in code reviews and in front of senior stakeholders. You'll drive adoption of new ways of working while keeping State Street's bar for resilience and trust.

Are you passionate about making a difference and helping others?
Would you like to work in a role that puts the customer at the heart of everything we do, making a genuine positive impact?
Then consider the role of a Progression Coach at Reed in Partnership!
This role is office based, but will involve travel across Essex & Hertfordshire also.

Who we are:
Reed's Employability Division aims to positively transform lives by helping individuals who are unemployed, economically inactive, or facing challenges such as health conditions, disabilities, or caring responsibilities to find sustainable employment. Through a wide range of tailored support services including one-to-one careers guidance, CV writing, interview preparation, and skills training, we have supported over 250,000 people on their journey into work.
The new Confident Futures programme, funded by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), is designed to support Universal Credit claimants with long-term health conditions. It is a voluntary programme focused on helping participants move closer to work by improving confident, wellbeing, skills, stability and readiness for work.
What is the role about?
A Progression Coach is responsible for the attraction, registration and progression of Participants to achieve placements. A Progression Coach will use a variety of techniques including effective diagnosis, individual coaching and training, action planning and Health & Wellbeing Support to provide intensive personal support to a caseload of up to 25 Participants. Progression Coaches will deliver our services both in fixed Reed in Partnership locations, co-location sites and where appropriate within community venues, to ensure our services are accessible to all.

Provides a good customer service to Participants including meeting and greeting Participants in a professional way.
•
Explains our service offering (details of the programme) including ensuring the Participant understands their rights and responsibilities (e.g. complaints & feedback process), whilst registering the Participant in accordance to contractual obligations and eligibility criteria.
•
Ensure Initial Assessments focus on getting to know the participant, understanding their motivation for joining the programme (if voluntary participation) and exploration of their aspirations and needs.
•
Identifies and utilises various approaches where appropriate such as visionary goal setting, and applicable financial incentives to sell the benefits of the programme and to adequately diagnose first level barriers.
Participant Progression
•
Develops and manages Participants job goals using creative techniques and deep level questioning as necessary for the Participants needs, to assist with diagnosis and progression.
•
Motivates, encourages and empowers Participants, identifying barriers, realistic job goals and social training needs, referring as appropriate to relevant support functions
•
Collaborate with local and specialist partners to provide wraparound/holistic support that addresses multiple/complex barriers (e.g. finance, housing, caring responsibilities).
•
Engage with local employers to source suitable work experience/volunteering opportunities and support inclusive recruitment/job-carving.
Training Delivery
•
Engage and empower Learners whilst delivering training sessions, with the aim of progressing them to achieve sustainable employment.
•
Awareness of and ability to adapt to a diverse range of learners and their learning needs and styles.
•
Follow lesson plans and activity guidance provided.
In Work Support
•
Conducts into work meeting to ensure appropriate support is in place to support Participant to commence and sustain in work e.g. childcare. Agree preferred in-work support contact e.g. frequency and method, and in-work action plan.
•
Mentors the Participant through new employment, including providing support with general work issues finances and tax credits.

A generous base salary (pro-rata for part time), and great flexibility with your working schedule, we offer training, development and progression opportunities. You will have access to the range of Reed in Partnership benefits, which include:
•
25 days annual leave (pro-rata for part time) plus statutory bank holidays
•
Reed Pension Scheme
•
Award Winning Management & Leadership training
•
Professional & Personal Development Funds
•
Bi-annual pay reviews
•
With the chance to dramatically make a difference to the local community, this role offers immense job satisfaction
•
Plus much more that can be found on our website
To be successful in this role, we are looking for someone with:
•
Experience of working in a customer facing environment, e.g. Customer Services Assistant, Retail Assistant
•
Practical experience of working directly with similar client groups. E.g. those with moderate to severe disabilities, mental health issues, severe barriers to work
•
Experience of working in a performance target driven environment.  Examples of such experience may include working on a similar contract, being a Recruitment Consultant or experience of Business Development roles, sales targets in a retail business or call…

About Salesforce
Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.
The Experience
The Forward Deployed Consultant owns a customer engagement end to end: from the executive business case, through rapid design and deployment of automated process solutions ("Blueprints") on the Agentforce platform, to a clean handoff to partners and client teams. You will advise enterprise leaders, quantify ROI, and map multi-year automation roadmaps.
You bring domain depth in supply chain, ERP, or finance operations processes, including where people patch over system gaps.
You will also roll up your sleeves to build, test, and iterate Blueprints with AI agents and prompting tools, proving value fast in live production.
You are customer-obsessed, strategic, and execution-focused, with the speed and quality to turn fragmented manual workflows into scalable, value-driven solutions.
What You'll Actually Be Doing
• Serve as the primary strategic advisor to enterprise stakeholders, building a deep understanding of business goals and operational pain points.
• Build business cases and define success criteria up front: KPIs such as cycle time and cost per transaction, with a measured baseline.
• Own multi-year roadmaps for process Blueprints and automation, balancing strategic direction with near-term execution.
• Present to executives in terms of their priorities; flag when work is off track early and plainly, with a fix, and drive to a decision.
• Lead structured discovery (workshops, process maps) and turn it into a solution design and a first working version in days to weeks.
• Automate business processes end to end (procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, supplier onboarding), deciding what stays in the ERP, what is automated around it, and what AI decides versus people.
• Build hands-on with AI agents and prompting tools: design prompts, structure outputs with schemas and examples, and debug and iterate when they fail.
• Identify integration points with core systems (REST, event-based), managing risks such as auth, latency, payload limits, and retries.
• Translate strategic goals into clear PRDs and technical acceptance criteria.
• Deliver in continuous build loops (design, build, validate, refine), where each loop proves value and expands scope toward AI-first operations.
• Lead an AI-first delivery experience, using AI agents and skills to accelerate requirements, build, testing, and documentation.
• Own delivery end to end through go-live: scoping, build, UAT, data migration, and cutover, managing scope change along the way.
• Cut scope to the highest-value slice(Day 1 Scope/MVP)) when needed to get live, and justify the trade-off to the customer.
• Design and run handoff processes, documentation, and enablement that transition ownership to implementation partners and customer teams.
• Set handoff guidelines, solution architecture documentation, and success criteria for sustained post-deployment success.

• 5+ years in Solutions Consulting, Forward Deployed roles, Strategic or Management Consulting, Product Management, Process Automation, or Business Analysis.

• Hands-on experience building AI or agent-based automation yourself, including prompt design, output structuring, and iterating on failures.
• Experience engaging enterprise executives in B2B SaaS to build business cases and long-term roadmaps.
• Proven track record owning engagements from discovery through go-live (UAT, data migration, cutover), not just POCs, followed by structured handoffs.
• Strong grounding in workflow mapping, process modeling, process improvement, and change management.
• Experience translating business requirements into automated workflows, PRDs, and user stories.
• Working knowledge of integration patterns (REST, SOAP, event-based) and common risks such as auth, latency, and payload limits.
• Track record of setting success KPIs and baselines up front and measuring outcomes after go-live.
• Executive presence: confident with skeptical executives and willing to deliver bad news early, with a plan.
Even Better If...
• Familiarity with the Salesforce platform ecosystem (APIs, platform services).
• Track record building or navigating partner ecosystems and implementation channels.
• Lean, Six Sigma, or related process improvement certification.
• Technical or business degree; MBA a plus.
Unleash Your Potential
When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

Be Yourself – Be a Bold Team Player – Be Leonardo
Once you’re part of the team, you’re part of the Leonardo community of over 55 hotels across the UK & Ireland!
The Receptionist will support the smooth running and objectives of the Front Office department. All members of the department work together to create memorable moments for guests, in line with both company and hotel-specific service standards, and collaborate closely with other departments within the hotel. You will act as an ambassador for your own hotel and the wider Leonardo Hotels estate, demonstrating the company vision, mission and values. At all times, you will treat others around you with respect, dignity and fairness.
As a Receptionist you’ll be a face of the hotel, so we want you to bring your warm and friendly personality to work with you every day. Take a deep breath because you’ll be stepping into a busy role! Working as part of a vibrant team, you’ll be an ambassador for the hotel as the first person our guests will meet. Whilst organising all aspects of the check-in and check-out processes, you’ll be offering guests the real 5-star treatment at our hotel!
If you’re our ideal Receptionist, you will:
• Be passionate to make a difference and eager to bring new ideas to the table
• Be courteous to guests and colleagues at all times
• Use your savvy knowledge to offer guidance and local recommendations for a great stay in the city
• Have top-notch organisational skills
• Be dependable, and a reassuring influence for guests
Some of the perks our Receptionist could enjoy include:
•
Special rates on Leonardo Hotel rooms across the UK & Europe
•
Company-wide recognition scheme: you could earn vouchers to spend on a wide range of high street shops
•
Talent referral scheme
•
Thank You Week: from ice cream trucks to yoga classes and lots in between!
•
Wellbeing Calendar
•
Ongoing job-related training programmes with clear paths for progression
We’re committed to creating a workplace where every individual—regardless of background, identity, or lived experience—is welcomed, valued, and respected for who they are. Belonging means embracing our differences and ensuring everyone feels seen, heard, and empowered.
Why come join us as a Receptionist?
We look after our colleagues just as well as we look after our guests. Our regular Learning Bites, “Come Join Us Guest Care” training and Wellbeing webinars all help your progress with us. With support on tap, top-notch practical training and clear progression you’ll be on track for a brilliant future in Hospitality!
